Standard: AR systems have functions to ensure AR operations occur without creating a hazardous condition. a. Boom Tanker. Tanker has the ability to reduce commanded delivery pressure, to advance boom state to contact, to send a disconnect signal to the receiver when commanded by the operator or automated system, and to transition the boom into and out of the stowed position. b. Drogue Tanker. Tanker has the ability to reduce commanded delivery pressure, to extend and retract the refueling hose and drogue, and to jettison the refueling hose and trailing components. c. Receptacle Receiver. Receiver has the ability to disconnect from the boom and to send a disconnect signal to the tanker when commanded by the crewmember or automated system, to reset the receptacle system state from disconnect to ready, to bypass the receptacle signal amplifier (if applicable), and to transition the receiver into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., open and close refueling door(s), transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic). d. Probe Receiver. Receiver has the ability to transition into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., probe extension and retraction, transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): Examination.
(1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Examination of specifications and design documentation verifies tanker has functions to reduce commanded delivery pressure, to advance boom state to contact, to send a disconnect signal to the receiver when commanded by the crewmember or automated system, and to transition the boom into and out of the stowed position. b. Drogue Tanker. Examination of specifications and design documentation verifies tanker has functions to reduce commanded delivery pressure, to extend and retract the refueling hose and drogue, and to jettison the refueling hose and trailing components. c. Receptacle Receiver. Examination of specifications and design documentation verifies receiver has functions to disconnect from the boom and to send a disconnect signal to the tanker when commanded by the crewmember or automated system, to reset the receptacle system state from disconnect to ready, to bypass the receptacle signal amplifier (if applicable), to transition the receiver into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., open and close refueling door(s), transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic). d. Probe Receiver. Examination of specifications and design documentation verifies receiver has functions to transition into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., probe extension and retraction, transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic). Analysis.
  (1) Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Analysis of tanker design, AR software logic and associated models verify tanker has the capability to reduce commanded delivery pressure, to advance boom state to contact, to send a disconnect signal to the receiver when commanded by the crewmember or automated system, and to transition the boom into and out of the stowed position. b. Drogue Tanker. Analysis of tanker design, AR software logic and associated models verify tanker has the capability to reduce commanded delivery pressure, to extend and retract the refueling hose and drogue, and to jettison the refueling hose and trailing components. c. Receptacle Receiver. Analysis of receiver design, AR software logic and associated models verify receiver has the capability to disconnect from the boom and to send a disconnect signal to the tanker when commanded by the crewmember or automated system, to reset the receptacle system state from disconnect to ready, to bypass the receptacle signal amplifier (if applicable), and to transition the receiver into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., open and close refueling door(s), transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic). d. Probe Receiver. Analysis of receiver design, AR software logic and associated models verify receiver has the capability to transition into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., probe extension and retraction, transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic). Test.
    (1) Lab test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Testing in a laboratory environment verifies fuel system delivers fuel at a reduced delivery pressure when commanded, boom state advances to contact when commanded and disconnect signal is sent via the signal coil when commanded by the crewmember or automated system. b. Drogue Tanker. Testing in a laboratory environment verifies fuel system delivers fuel at a reduced delivery pressure when commanded. c. Receptacle Receiver. Testing in a laboratory environment verifies receptacle latches release the boom nozzle and a disconnect signal is sent via the signal coil when commanded by the crewmember or automated system, the receptacle system state resets from disconnect to ready when commanded, receptacle signal amplifier can be bypassed (if applicable), and receiver transitions into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., open and close refueling door(s), transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic) when commanded. d. Probe Receiver. Testing in a laboratory environment verifies receiver transitions into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., probe extension and retraction, transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic) when commanded.
    (2) Ground test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Air vehicle ground testing verifies fuel system delivers fuel at a reduced delivery pressure when commanded. b. Drogue Tanker. On air vehicle ground testing verifies fuel system delivers fuel at a reduced delivery pressure when commanded. c. Receptacle Receiver. Air vehicle ground testing verifies receiver transitions into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., open and close refueling door(s), transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic) when commanded. d. Probe Receiver. Air vehicle ground testing verifies receiver transitions into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., probe extension and retraction, transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic) when commanded. Prior to entering operational test/operations, verify the standard by the above and following method(s): Test.
    (3) Flight test: Verify the standard by the following: a. Boom Tanker. Flight test verifies tanker fuel system delivers fuel at a reduced delivery pressure when commanded, boom state advances to contact when commanded, disconnect signal is sent to the receiver when commanded by the operator or automated system, and the boom transitions into and out of the stowed position when commanded. b. Drogue Tanker. Flight test verifies tanker fuel system delivers fuel at a reduced delivery pressure when commanded, the refueling hose and drogue are extended and retracted when commanded, and the refueling hose and trailing components are jettisoned when commanded. c. Receptacle Receiver. Flight test verifies receptacle latches release the boom nozzle and a disconnect signal is sent to the tanker when commanded by the operator or automated system, the receptacle system state resets from disconnect to ready when commanded, receptacle signal amplifier can be bypassed (if applicable), and receiver transitions into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., open and close refueling door(s), transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic) when commanded. d. Probe Receiver. Flight test verifies receiver transitions into and out of refueling configuration (e.g., probe extension and retraction, transition flight control law logic, fuel transfer logic) when commanded.
